## §9.1.1: The Cascade Principle, *Partialkomposition* & Sieve States (SM-59a, SM-60) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: HISTORICAL EXEGESIS OF SM SECTION 7.5 (SM, PP. 145–205; PP. 180–183, EQS. 59–60a)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-down}
**Historical Vignette (*The Stuttgart Astronautical Address*) & Switchboard Intuition:**
Historical discussions of Heim's manuscripts belong to the period's wider search for algebraic field symmetries; here they serve as context only, while the gauge constructions below stand on their own formal definitions. The symmetric, skew, cross-dimensional, and internal blocks of a $6\times 6$ metric act as channels on one **geometric switchboard**, where different physical roles correspond to typed blocks of the same tensor object.
:::

* **From Coordinate Channels to Unified Spacetime:** Chapter 8 showed that continuous parameters on $\mathcal{M}_n = (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n$ decompose via Grothendieck nuclearity. Yet macroscopic geometry cannot emerge in a single unmediated burst without infinite curvature stresses.
* **Strukturkaskade (SM §7.5, pp. 180–183):** Spacetime geometry is the convergent fixed point of a hierarchical assembly indexed by cascade tiers $\kaskadenstufe \in \{1, \dots, M\}$:
  * **Kaskadenbasis ($\kaskadenstufe = 1$):** Ensemble of $L_1 = \binom{n}{\omega_1}$ basal partial metrics ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_{(\gamma_1)}^{(1)}$ generated by tier $F_1$ of the *Quantitätssyntrix* on $R_n$.
  * **Partialkomposition (SM Eq. 60, p. 182):** Non-linear assembly integrating Christoffel connections and curvature couplings:
    $$
    {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_{(\gamma_\alpha)}^{(\alpha)} = \mathfrak{f}\!\left[ \left( {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_{(\gamma_{\alpha-1})}^{(\alpha-1)} \right)^{\omega_\alpha} \right], \quad 1 \le \gamma_\alpha \le L_\alpha = \binom{L_{\alpha-1}}{\omega_\alpha}, \quad 1 \le \alpha \le M \tag{SM-60}
    $$
  * **Kaskadenspitze ($\kaskadenstufe = M$, SM Eq. 60a):** Terminates at $L_M = 1, \omega_M = \omega = n/2$ into the unified metric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}$ via an **analytischer Syllogismus** (SM, p. 180) of ascending conditionality (*Bedingtheit*).

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Proposition 9.1 (Closed-Form Sieve State Partition, SM Eqs. 59 & 59a):**
With sieve-state sum $(\omega - p)' \coloneqq \sum_{l=1}^{\omega-p}\binom{\omega - p}{l} = 2^{\omega - p} - 1$ $\text{(SM-59a)}$, the total symmetric decoupled metric-state count from SM Eq. 59 is:
$$
Z_+ = 2\left(\sum_{p=0}^{\omega-1}(2^{\omega-p}-1)\binom{\omega}{p} + 1\right) = 2\left(3^\omega - 2^\omega + 1\right) \tag{SM-59}
$$
For the physical condensation dimension $n = 6$ ($\omega = 3$), this evaluates to $Z_+ = 2(27 - 8 + 1) = \mathbf{40}$.
:::

## §9.1.2–9.1.4: Non-Hermitian *Hermetrie* (SM-37), *Strukturassoziation* & *Übergangskriterium* {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: NON-HERMITIAN METRICS (SM, PP. 145–179), CONNECTION TENSORS (PP. 157, 182) &amp; TRANSITION CRITERION (PP. 185, 201–206)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

* **Non-Hermitian *Kompositionsfeld* (SM §7.4, Eq. 37):** Instead of discarding metric skew-symmetry as unphysical, Heim decomposes ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}$ into symmetric and anti-symmetric sectors:
  $$
  {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ + {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-, \qquad {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ = ({}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+)^\times, \qquad {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_- = -({}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-)^\times \tag{SM-37}
  $$
  * **Symmetric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+$ ($21$ potentials on $R_6$):** Riemannian curvature, gravitational acceleration, and spatial distances.
  * **Skew-Symmetric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-$ ($15$ potentials on $R_6$):** Electromagnetic field-strength vortices, chiral torsion, and rotational momentum fluxes.
* **Ontic Structural Realism (OSR):** Realizes Steven French's *OSR* (relational structures rather than forces in a container) and Bas van Fraassen's *Scientific Representation* on $R_6 = R_4 \times S_2$: $\dim_{\mathbb{R}}(\operatorname{Mat}_{6\times 6}) = 36 = 21 + 15$.
* **Strukturassoziation (SM, pp. 157, 182):** Mediated by the **Fundamentalkondensor** ($\fundamentalkondensor \equiv \Gamma_{kl}^i$):
  * **Korrelationstensor ($\korrelationstensor$, SM Eq. 52):** Symmetric cross-metric connections generating $n$-ary configurations (*Binär-*, *Ternär-*, *Quartärfelder*).
  * **Koppelungstensor ($\koppelungstensor$, SM Eq. 53):** Skew-symmetric connection & non-commuting metric commutator difference tensor.
* **Kontraktionsgesetze ($\kappa$, SM p. 185) & *Übergangskriterium* (SM §7.6, Eq. 64, p. 206):**
  $$
  \left( \frac{\chi}{\tau^{(p-2)/2}} \right) \sqrt{|g_{(p)}|} = 1 \tag{SM-64}
  $$
  Marks the critical determinant threshold where continuous differential calculus collapses into discrete metronic cells ($x_i = N_i\alpha_i$, Chapter 10).

:::

## §9.2.1: Fréchet Metric Bundles $\operatorname{Met}(\mathcal{M})$ & Mixed-Variant Transport {.smaller auto-animate=true}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATIONS — NON-HERMITIAN METRIC BUNDLES &amp; MIXED-VARIANT TRANSPORT (SM, PP. 159–160)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Scholium 9.2 (Meta-Theoretic Justification: Non-Hermitian Metric Bundles):**
Why formalize Heim's *Kompositionsfeld* as ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ + {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-$ on a Fréchet manifold $\operatorname{Met}(\mathcal{M})$?
1. **Unified Geometrization of Gravity & Electromagnetism:** Symmetric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+$ encodes Levi-Civita spacetime curvature (gravity), while skew-symmetric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-$ encodes the field-strength 2-form $F_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu A_\nu - \partial_\nu A_\mu$ (electromagnetism/torsion) without ad hoc fields.
2. **Banach Fixed-Point Convergence:** $(\Gamma_b^0(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{Sym}^2(T^*\mathcal{M})), \|\cdot\|_{C^0_b})$ is a complete Banach space; modeling $\Phi_M = \bigcirc_{\alpha=1}^M(\kappa_\alpha\mathcal{T}_\alpha)$ as a strict contraction proves unique convergence to ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 9.3 (The Space of Metric Bundles $\operatorname{Met}(\mathcal{M})$):**
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a smooth $n$-dimensional manifold with $n = 2\omega$.
1. **Non-Hermitian Metric Bundle:** $\operatorname{Met}(\mathcal{M}) \subset \Gamma(\mathcal{M}, T^*\mathcal{M} \otimes T^*\mathcal{M})$ equipped with the $C_b^\infty$ Fréchet topology, where each non-degenerate metric decomposes uniquely:
   $$
   {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ + {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-, \quad {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ \in \Gamma(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{Sym}^2(T^*\mathcal{M})), \quad {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_- \in \Gamma(\mathcal{M}, \Lambda^2(T^*\mathcal{M}))
   $$
2. **Connection Affine Space:** $\operatorname{Conn}(\mathcal{M})$ is an affine space modeled on $\Omega^1(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{End}(T\mathcal{M}))$.
:::

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .blur-in}
**Remark (Heim's Mixed-Variant Covariant Derivative & Transposition Argument, SM pp. 159–160):**
For a tensor with $\mu$ covariant and $m-\mu$ contravariant indices:
$$
A_{i_1\cdots i_\mu,k}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{i}_m} = \frac{\partial A_{i_1\cdots i_\mu}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{i}_m}}{\partial x^{\underline{k}}} - \sum_{\lambda=1}^{\mu}\begin{Bmatrix}s\\i_\lambda,k\end{Bmatrix}A_{i_1\cdots s\cdots i_\mu}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{i}_m} + \sum_{\lambda=\mu+1}^{m}\begin{Bmatrix}i_\lambda\\s\;k\end{Bmatrix}A_{i_1\cdots i_\mu}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{s}\cdots\underline{i}_m}
$$
For a parallel-transported covariant vector, subtracting its index-transposed form yields:
$$
\frac{\partial A_i}{\partial x^{\underline{k}}} - \frac{\partial A_k}{\partial x^{\underline{i}}} = A_s\left(\begin{Bmatrix}s\\i\;k\end{Bmatrix} - \begin{Bmatrix}s\\k\;i\end{Bmatrix}\right)
$$
*Epistemic Caution:* This identity contracts the skew connection with $A_s$; a nonzero skew connection requires an explicit nonvanishing-curl and nondegeneracy premise.
:::

## §9.2.2: The 36-Component Non-Hermitian *Hermetrie* Matrix on $R_6 = R_4 \times S_2$ {.smaller auto-animate=true}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: THE 36-COMPONENT HERMETRY PARTITION ON ANHOLONOMIC FRAMES (SCHOLIUM 9.4, DEF. 9.5 &amp; FIGS. 9.2, 9.4)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="47%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Scholium 9.4 & Definition 9.5 (The 36-Component Non-Hermitian Hermetry Matrix on $R_6 = R_4 \times S_2$):**
On the 6-dimensional physical sub-manifold $R_6 = R_4 \times S_2$, the non-Hermitian metric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ + {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-$ has 36 real components partitioned into:
$$
\dim_{\mathbb{R}}(\operatorname{Mat}_{6 \times 6}) = 36 = \underbrace{21}_{\text{Symmetric } {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+} + \underbrace{15}_{\text{Skew-Symmetric } {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-}
$$
1. **21 Symmetric Components (${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+$):**
   * **10** spacetime metric potentials $g_{\mu\nu}$ ($R_4 \times R_4$: Einstein gravity),
   * **8** Kaluza–Klein gravito-electromagnetic potentials ($R_4 \times S_2$),
   * **3** mesobaric scalars ($S_2 \times S_2$: internal organizational gauge).
2. **15 Skew-Symmetric Components (${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-$):**
   * **6** electromagnetic vorticity components $F_{\mu\nu}$ ($R_4 \times R_4$: Maxwell field),
   * **8** chiral spin-torsion potentials ($R_4 \times S_2$: inertial mass flux),
   * **1** entelechial commutator $[\partial_5, \partial_6]$ ($S_2 \times S_2$: aeonic update).
:::

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Remark (Toy Example: 4D Non-Hermitian Metric with Maxwell Vorticity):**
On $\mathcal{M} = \mathbb{R}^4$ with coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, consider a uniform magnetic field $B$ along $z$:
$$
{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & B & 0 \\ 0 & -B & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} = \underbrace{\operatorname{diag}(-1, 1, 1, 1)}_{{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ \text{ (Minkowski Gravity)}} + \underbrace{B\,(dx \wedge dy)}_{{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_- \text{ (Magnetic Vorticity } F_{xy}=B\text{)}}
$$
Electromagnetism appears directly as an intrinsic skew-symmetric sector of ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}$.
:::

## §9.3.1: Palatini Cross-Metric Connection Decomposition (Theorem 9.6, SM-53) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: DERIVED MATHEMATICAL THEOREMS — CROSS-METRIC CONNECTION &amp; KOPPELUNGSTENSOR Q (THM. 9.6, SM EQ. 53)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Theorem 9.6 (Palatini Cross-Metric Connection Decomposition Theorem, SM Eq. 53):**
Let $\{g_{(\gamma)}\}_{\gamma=1}^\omega \subset \operatorname{Met}(\mathcal{M})$ be $\omega$ smooth non-Hermitian partial metrics on $\mathcal{M}$, and $g \coloneqq \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega g_{(\gamma)}$ their composite sum metric with right-inverse $g^{is}$ ($g_{sa}g^{ak} = \delta_s^k$). Let $[s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)} \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}(\partial_k g_{(\gamma)sl} + \partial_l g_{(\gamma)ks} - \partial_s g_{(\gamma)kl})$.
1. **Exact Algebraic Decomposition (SM Eq. 53):** The composite second-kind Christoffel symbols $\Gamma_{kl}^i = \left\{\begin{smallmatrix}i\\kl\end{smallmatrix}\right\} \coloneqq g^{is}[s\,k\,l]$ decompose identically as:
   $$
   \left\{ \begin{smallmatrix} i \\ k \, l \end{smallmatrix} \right\} \;=\; \sum_{\mu=1}^\omega \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega \left( \begin{Bmatrix} i \\ k \; l \end{Bmatrix}^{(\mu)}_{(\gamma)} + \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \begin{Bmatrix} m \\ k \; l \end{Bmatrix}^{(\mu)}_{(\gamma)} \right) \tag{SM-53}
   $$
   where $\begin{Bmatrix}i\\kl\end{Bmatrix}_{(\gamma)}^{(\mu)} \coloneqq g_{(\mu)}^{\dagger,is}[s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)}$ is the cross-metric connection (*Korrelationstensor*) and the **Koppelungstensor** is the exact algebraic difference tensor:
   $$
   \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \;\coloneqq\; g^{is} g_{(\mu)sm} - \frac{1}{\omega}\delta_m^i
   $$
2. **Decoupling Criterion:** $\mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \equiv 0 \iff g_{(\mu)} = \frac{1}{\omega}g\;\;\forall \mu \in \{1,\dots,\omega\}$ (homothety alignment). Anisotropy or misalignment forces $\mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)} \ne \mathbf{0}$, generating non-linear cross-metric interactions.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Theorem 9.6 (Exact 3-Step Algebraic Factorization):**
1. *Linearity of 1st-kind symbols:* $[s\,k\,l] = \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega [s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)} \implies \left\{\begin{smallmatrix}i\\kl\end{smallmatrix}\right\} = \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega g^{is}[s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)}$.
2. *Resolution of identity:* Using $\delta_a^s = g_{(\mu)am}g_{(\mu)}^{\dagger,ms}$, insert $\sum_{\mu=1}^\omega \delta_a^s$:
   $$
   g^{is}[s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)} = \sum_{\mu=1}^\omega (g^{ia}g_{(\mu)am})\begin{Bmatrix}m\\kl\end{Bmatrix}_{(\gamma)}^{(\mu)} = \sum_{\mu=1}^\omega \left(\frac{1}{\omega}\delta_m^i + \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i\right)\begin{Bmatrix}m\\kl\end{Bmatrix}_{(\gamma)}^{(\mu)}
   $$
3. *Homothety limit:* If $g_{(\mu)} = \frac{1}{\omega}g$, then $g^{ia}g_{(\mu)am} = \frac{1}{\omega}g^{ia}g_{am} = \frac{1}{\omega}\delta_m^i \implies \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \equiv 0$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

## §9.3.1b: Contortion Tensor $\mathbf{K}_{kl}^i$, Curvature Splitting & Ricci Density Curl {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: ALGEBRAIC CONTORTION TENSOR (DEF. 9.13), CURVATURE SPLITTING &amp; RICCI VOLUME-DENSITY CURL (LEMMA 9.7, SM-51)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Definition 9.13 (Algebraic Contortion Tensor in Non-Hermitian Palatini Gravity):**
Let $T_{kl}^i \coloneqq \Gamma_{[kl]}^i = \frac{1}{2}(\Gamma_{kl}^i - \Gamma_{lk}^i)$ be the metric torsion tensor of the non-Hermitian connection. The **Contortion Tensor** $\mathbf{K}_{kl}^i$ is the unique linear tensor satisfying:
$$
\Gamma_{kl}^i = \left\{ \begin{smallmatrix} i \\ k \, l \end{smallmatrix} \right\}_{{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+} + \mathbf{K}_{kl}^i, \qquad K_{ikl} \coloneqq g_{is} \mathbf{K}_{kl}^s = \frac{1}{2}\left( T_{ikl} + T_{lik} - T_{kli} \right)
$$
where $T_{ikl} \coloneqq g_{is}T_{kl}^s$. If the skew-symmetric metric sector vanishes (${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_- \equiv \mathbf{0} \implies T_{kl}^i \equiv 0$), then $K_{ikl} \equiv 0$, recovering the torsion-free Levi-Civita connection.
:::

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Remark (Curvature Decomposition Under a Contortion $\Gamma = \Gamma^{(+)} + \mathbf{K}$):**
With $R^i{}_{klm} = \partial_l\Gamma^i_{km} - \partial_m\Gamma^i_{kl} + \Gamma^i_{sl}\Gamma^s_{km} - \Gamma^i_{sm}\Gamma^s_{kl}$, direct expansion yields the exact curvature splitting:
$$
R^i{}_{klm}(\Gamma) = R^{(+)i}{}_{klm} + \nabla^{(+)}_l\mathbf{K}^i{}_{km} - \nabla^{(+)}_m\mathbf{K}^i{}_{kl} + \mathbf{K}^i{}_{sl}\mathbf{K}^s{}_{km} - \mathbf{K}^i{}_{sm}\mathbf{K}^s{}_{kl}
$$
*Epistemic Note:* This is an exact differential-geometric curvature decomposition; an Einstein–Maxwell physical interpretation requires additional field equations and a justified source ansatz.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Lemma 9.7 (Determinant Curl Term in the Ricci Splitting, SM Eq. 51, p. 179):**
Let $w \coloneqq \sqrt{|\det g|}$ denote the metric volume density and $\llcorner_l w$ Heim's covariant volume-density derivative. The common $2\times 2$ operator-determinant term in the symmetric and skew Ricci components expands as a curl-like contribution:
$$
\frac{1}{2} \begin{vmatrix} \partial_l & \partial_k \\ \frac{1}{w}\llcorner_l & \frac{1}{w}\llcorner_k \end{vmatrix} w = \frac{1}{2}\left[ \partial_l\!\left(\frac{1}{w}\llcorner_k w\right) - \partial_k\!\left(\frac{1}{w}\llcorner_l w\right) \right] \tag{SM-51}
$$
:::

## §9.3.1c: Non-Hermitian Palatini Conservation (Thm. 9.8, SM-49) & No-Go Firewall {.smaller transition="concave"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B &amp; CARNAP SCHOLIUM 9.1: PALATINI COMPATIBILITY, EINSTEIN CONSERVATION (SM-49) &amp; DAMOUR–DESER–MCCARTHY NO-GO</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Theorem 9.8 (Non-Hermitian Palatini Conservation Constraint & Compatibility, SM Eq. 49):**
Let $(\mathcal{M}, {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}})$ have canonical first-second Ricci contraction ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}}_{kl} \coloneqq R^m_{\;\;kml}$, right-inverse $g_{ia}g^{ak} = \delta_i^k$, and two-sided scalar curvature $\mathrm{R} \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}g^{kl}({}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}}_{kl} + {}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}}_{lk})$.
1. **Divergence-Free Conservation Identity (SM Eq. 49):** In the locally geodesic frame signature $(s_1=6, s_2=6)$ where $\Gamma=0$ (SM Eq. 42, p. 164), the non-Hermitian Einstein tensor $\mathbf{G} \coloneqq {}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}} - \frac{1}{2}{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}\mathrm{R}$ satisfies:
   $$
   \operatorname{div}_{\bar{g}} \left[ \llcorner_{(-)}^{(6, 6)}\!\left( {}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}} - \frac{1}{2}{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} \mathrm{R} \right) \right] \coloneqq \operatorname{sp}\llcorner_{(-)}^{(6,6)}\!\left( {}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}} - \frac{1}{2}{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} \mathrm{R} \right) = \mathbf{0} \tag{SM-49}
   $$
2. **Palatini Metric-Torsion Compatibility Equations:** Varying $S[g,\Gamma] = \int_{\mathcal{M}} d^nx\sqrt{-\det g}\,g^{ik}R_{ik}(\Gamma) + \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}\sqrt{|g_\partial|}g^{ik}K_{ik}(\Gamma)d^{n-1}x$ independently with respect to $\Gamma_{kl}^i$ yields:
   $$
   \nabla_k g_{lm} - T^s_{\;\;km} g_{ls} + \frac{1}{n-1} g_{lm} T^s_{\;\;ks} - \frac{1}{n-1} g_{km} T^s_{\;\;ls} = 0
   $$
   algebraically fixing all $n^3$ connection degrees of freedom in terms of $g_{ab}$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Theorem 9.8 (Generalized Differential Bianchi Contraction):**
Under $\nabla$ with torsion $T_{kl}^i = \Gamma_{[kl]}^i$, curvature satisfies the generalized differential Bianchi identity:
$$
\nabla_{[m} R^i_{\phantom{i}|k|jl]} = T_{[mj}^s R^i_{\phantom{i}|k|sl]}
$$
Contracting $i$ with $j$ gives the contracted Bianchi identity for ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}}_{kl} = R^m_{\;\;kml}$. Applying $\operatorname{sp}\llcorner_{(-)}^{(6,6)}$ eliminates symmetric divergence residuals and isolates stationary vorticity flux, yielding $\operatorname{sp}\llcorner_{(-)}^{(6,6)}({}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}} - \frac{1}{2}{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}\mathrm{R}) = \mathbf{0}$. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §9.3.1d: Tensor Densities, Divergence Splitting & the $(n-2)$ Theorem (SM-41, 44, 46, 46a) {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: VECTOR DENSITIES (LEMMA 9.9), DIVERGENCE SPLITTING &amp; (n−2) THEOREM (THM. 9.10), KRONECKER NON-METRICITY (THM. 9.11)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Lemma 9.9 (Covariant Derivative of a Contravariant Vector Density, SM pp. 167–168):**
For a weight-$+1$ contravariant vector density $\underline{A}^{\underline{i}} \coloneqq p A^{\underline{i}}$, the positive-sign operator selector acts as:
$$
\llcorner_{(+),k}^{(1)}\underline{A}^{\underline{i}} \coloneqq \frac{\partial\underline{A}^{\underline{i}}}{\partial x^{\underline{k}}} + \underline{A}^{\underline{s}}\begin{Bmatrix}i\\sk\end{Bmatrix} - \underline{A}^{\underline{i}}\begin{Bmatrix}s\\sk\end{Bmatrix}_{+}
$$
**Lemma 9.12 (Metric Derivative, Inverse & Christoffel Trace, SM Eq. 41):**
For symmetric $g_{+ik}$ with Levi-Civita symbols $\Gamma^m_{+il}$: $\partial_l g_{+ik} = g_{+km}\Gamma^m_{+il} + g_{+im}\Gamma^m_{+kl}$, $\partial_l g_+^{ik} = -g_+^{jk}\Gamma^i_{+jl} - g_+^{ij}\Gamma^k_{+jl}$, and the determinant derivative gives $\partial_l \ln\sqrt{|g_+|} = \Gamma^k_{+kl}$ $\text{(SM-41)}$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 9.10 (Metric Density Divergence and the $(n-2)$ Theorem, SM Eqs. 46 & 46a):**
Let $w \coloneqq \sqrt{|\det g|}$ and $\underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}} \coloneqq w\bar{\mathbf{A}}$.
1. **Divergence Splitting (SM Eq. 46):** Isolating vector divergence from contracted skew torsion trace:
   $$
   \operatorname{sp} \llcorner_{(+)}^{(1)} \underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}} + \operatorname{sp} \llcorner_{(+)}^{(2)} \underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}} = 2 \operatorname{div}_n \underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}}, \qquad \operatorname{sp} \llcorner_{(+)}^{(1)} \underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}} - \operatorname{sp} \llcorner_{(+)}^{(2)} \underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}} = 2 \underline{A}^{\underline{k}} \begin{Bmatrix} s \\ sk \end{Bmatrix}_- \tag{SM-46}
   $$
2. **The $(n-2)$ Density Theorem (SM Eq. 46a):** Contracting $g_{ik}$ against the inverse metric density $\underline{g}^{\underline{ik}} \coloneqq w g^{\underline{ik}}$:
   $$
   g_{ik} \llcorner_{(+),l}^{(1,2)} \underline{g}^{\underline{ik}} = (n - 2) \llcorner_l w, \qquad \llcorner_l w \coloneqq \frac{\partial w}{\partial x^{\underline{l}}} - w\begin{Bmatrix}s\\sl\end{Bmatrix}_+ \tag{SM-46a}
   $$
   Vanishes identically for $n=2$, equals $2\llcorner_l w$ for $n=4$, and evaluates to $4\llcorner_l w$ in physical condensation dimension $n=6$.
:::

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .blur-in}
**Theorem 9.11 (Non-Hermitian Non-Metricity on the Kronecker Delta, SM Eq. 44, p. 165):**
Heim's mixed-signature operator selector acts nontrivially on the unit tensor for off-diagonal signatures ($\varepsilon \ne \chi$): $\llcorner_{(\pm)}^{(\varepsilon),(\chi)}\delta_i^l \sim (1 - \delta_{\varepsilon\chi})$ $\text{(SM-44)}$, contrasting with the vanishing Levi-Civita derivative of $\delta_i^l$.
:::

## §9.3.2: DeTurck Parabolic Regularization & Sobolev $H^s$ Apex Convergence (Thm. 9.14) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: CONTRACTION DYNAMICS, DETURCK GAUGE FIXING &amp; SOBOLEV FIXED-POINT APEX CONVERGENCE (THM. 9.14, FIG. 9.6)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .fade-down}
**Why Naive Approaches Fail III: Ricci Flow's Diffeomorphism Degeneracy**
The unmodified Ricci-flow operator is **not strongly parabolic**: infinitesimal coordinate changes lie in the kernel of its principal symbol. Introducing the **DeTurck vector field** relative to background metric $\bar{g}$:
$$
V^k = g^{pq}\bigl(\Gamma_{pq}^k(g) - \Gamma_{pq}^k(\bar{g})\bigr)
$$
adds $\mathcal{L}_V g = \nabla_i V_j + \nabla_j V_i$, removing the principal-symbol degeneracy so $\sigma_\xi(\mathcal{T}(g))h_{ij} = \|\xi\|_g^2 h_{ij}$ becomes strictly elliptic and strongly parabolic.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Theorem 9.14 (Palatini Connection Uniqueness & Sobolev Fixed-Point Convergence):**
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be an $n$-dimensional compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, and fix $\bar{g} \in \operatorname{Met}^+(\mathcal{M})$.
1. **Unique Palatini Resolution:** Under the Einstein–Kaufman transposition constraint and ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}}^{(2)} \equiv 0$, Palatini variation uniquely fixes $\Gamma_{kl}^i$ in terms of ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}$ and $\mathbf{K}_{kl}^i$ (Thm. 9.8).
2. **DeTurck-Modified Cascade Operator:** Let $\mathcal{T}(g)_{ij} \coloneqq -2R_{ij}(g) + \nabla_i V_j + \nabla_j V_i$. For Sobolev index $s > \frac{n}{2} + 2$, the heat-regularized cascade operator:
   $$
   \mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}} \;\coloneqq\; e^{-\tau_M(\Delta_{\bar{g}} + c_0 I)} \circ \mathcal{T} \;\colon\; H^s(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{Sym}^2 T^*\mathcal{M}) \longrightarrow H^s(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{Sym}^2 T^*\mathcal{M})
   $$
   is a **strict Banach contraction** on $\mathbf{B}_{H^s}(\bar{g}, \delta)$ for $\tau_M \ge \tau_M^*$:
   $$
   \|\mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}}(g_1) - \mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}}(g_2)\|_{H^s} \;\le\; k_M \|g_1 - g_2\|_{H^s}, \qquad k_M \coloneqq C_{\text{heat}}C_{\text{geom}}(\bar{g},\delta)\frac{e^{-c_0\tau_M}}{\tau_M} < 1
   $$
3. **Unique Smooth Apex Metric:** By the Banach Fixed-Point Theorem and elliptic regularity bootstrapping, $g^{(m+1)} = \mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}}(g^{(m)})$ converges geometrically in $H^s$ to a unique ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty \in \bigcap_{k=s}^\infty H^k(\mathcal{M}) = C^\infty(\mathcal{M})$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

## §9.3.3: Unsatisfiability of Literal SM-61 (Thm. 9.15) & Metronic Transition Criterion (SM-64) {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B &amp; STRATUM C HYPOTHESIS: UNSATISFIABILITY OF LITERAL SM-61 (THM. 9.15) &amp; SINGULARITY BREAKDOWN (DEF. 9.16, THM. 9.17)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Theorem 9.15 (Unsatisfiability of Literal Formula 61) & Proof:**
Heim's SM Eq. 61 specifies $L_1 = \binom{n}{\omega_1}$ ($1 \le \omega_1 < n$), $L_\alpha = \binom{L_{\alpha-1}}{\omega_\alpha}$, and apex order $\omega_M = n/2$. **Under the apex condition $L_M = 1$, the literal cascade equalities are inconsistent for every $n \ge 2$.**
* *Proof:* Since $\binom{m}{k} \ge m$ for $1 \le k < m$, we have $L_1 = \binom{n}{\omega_1} \ge n$ and $L_{M-1} \ge L_1 \ge n$. But $L_M = \binom{L_{M-1}}{\omega_M} = 1$ forces $\omega_M = L_{M-1} \ge n$, contradicting $\omega_M = n/2$ for $n \ge 2$. $\blacksquare$

**Carnap Scholium 9.2 (Explication of Formula 61 via Rank-Filtered Upper Bound):**
$$
L_\alpha \;\coloneqq\; \operatorname{rank}\!\left(\kappa_\alpha\!\left(\operatorname{Sym}^{\omega_\alpha}(F_{\alpha-1})\right)\right) \;\le\; \binom{L_{\alpha-1}}{\omega_\alpha}
$$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 9.16 (Geometric Cell-Volume Derivation of the Transition Criterion, SM Eq. 64):**
On an active $p$-dimensional sub-manifold $(\mathcal{M}_p, g_{(p)})$, the cell quantum $\tau$ satisfies $\Delta V_p = \sqrt{|g_{(p)}|}\prod_{i=1}^p \Delta x^{\underline{i}} = \tau$. With $\Delta x^{\underline{i}} = \chi_i\sqrt[p]{\tau}$ and $\chi \coloneqq \prod_{i=1}^p \chi_i$, $\tau$ cancels on both sides ($\tau = \tau\chi\sqrt{|g_{(p)}|}$), yielding the **Metronic Transition Criterion**:
$$
\chi \sqrt{|g_{(p)}|} = 1, \qquad {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_{(p)} = \text{const} \quad \left(\text{or }\frac{\chi}{\tau^{(p-2)/(2p)}}\sqrt{|g_{(p)}|} = 1\text{ for }[\tau]=L^2\right) \tag{SM-64}
$$
:::

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .glow-pulse}
**Theorem 9.17 (Singularity Breakdown of Continuous Cascades — Stratum C Hypothesis, $\mathbf{S_0}, \mathbf{E_2}$):**
If the metric gradient breaches $\|\nabla {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}\|_{\text{crit}} \ge \frac{1}{\sqrt{\tau}}$ (or $\tau^{-1/p}$), Christoffel symbols $\Gamma \sim g^{-1}\partial g$ diverge in $\ddot{x}^i = -\Gamma_{kl}^i\dot{x}^k\dot{x}^l$, rendering smooth $C^2$ geodesics unextendable and positing the fracture of $\mathcal{M}$ into discrete metronic cells $x_i = N_i\alpha_i$ ($\alpha_i \coloneqq \chi_i\sqrt{\tau}, N_i \in \mathbb{Z}$) on lattice $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n$ (Chapter 10). $\blacksquare$
:::
